title: AI Slop Shame Mirror
oneLiner: A playful self-audit booth that tells creators whether a post feels like disposable AI slop or something a human would actually share.
targetUser: Creators, founders, newsletter writers, indie makers, educators, and marketers who use AI drafts but fear audience embarrassment or “slop” backlash.
keyUx: Paste a draft post, landing hero, short-video script, newsletter intro, or product update; the app highlights generic phrases, fake-depth signals, over-polished tone, missing lived detail, and shareability hooks, then gives a before/after “less slop, more soul” makeover card.
externalSignals: Signal 1 — Reddit r/AiForSmallBusiness — What AI tools are actually staying in your stack for 2026? — https://www.reddit.com/r/AiForSmallBusiness/comments/1qq03we/what_ai_tools_are_actually_staying_in_your_stack/

Signal 6 — Reddit r/technology — Microsoft Satya Nadella wants people to stop saying AI slop in 2026 — https://www.reddit.com/r/technology/comments/1q2449l/microsofts_satya_nadella_wants_you_to_stop_saying/
stitchPrompt: Design a playful creator self-audit product called AI Slop Shame Mirror for creators, founders, newsletter writers, indie makers, educators, and marketers who use AI drafts but fear audience embarrassment or “slop” backlash. Users should paste a draft post, landing hero, short-video script, newsletter intro, or product update, then highlight generic phrases, fake-depth signals, over-polished tone, missing lived detail, and shareability hooks, and generate a before/after “less slop, more soul” makeover card. Include a draft paste stage, slop smell score, generic phrase highlighter, human-detail injection prompts, audience cringe meter, before/after makeover card, and shareable anti-slop badge. Design direction: use a playful-experimental aesthetic with bold mirror-booth composition, cheeky but readable warning stickers, neon annotation marks, expressive cringe meters, and a highly shareable makeover card so the product feels like a memorable portfolio experiment about reputation anxiety, not a bland grammar checker.
